idiom_name: Vapor Middleware / AsyncMiddleware in the responder chain
implementation_notes: Vapor inserts middleware into the responder chain between client and route handler: conform to `Middleware` (or `AsyncMiddleware` for async/await) with `respond(to:chainingTo:)`, validate the request and then either throw Abort(.badRequest) or call next.respond(to:) - not calling next is the rejection. Register with `app.middleware.use(...)` so all routes are covered (or `app.grouped(...)` for a route group); registration order is the request order and the reverse for responses, replacing a hand-written interceptor chain. Vapor's responder chain makes the layer explicit, and validators written as plain functions can be tested without booting the application.
pitfalls: Route-group middleware runs after application middleware, and middleware registered on a group does not apply to routes added elsewhere; register validation at application scope and test the groups inherit it.
Blocking work in the EventLoopFuture `Middleware` variant ties up an event-loop thread; use `AsyncMiddleware` or shift CPU-heavy validation off the loop.
Throwing Abort inside middleware bypasses later request handling as intended but also skips the remaining chain's response processing; keep the error contract in the app's default error middleware.
